inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 reported revenue 123,707 less an ESTIMATED ~6,800 for Versant (cable networks spun 2 Jan 2026). Comcast did not restate comparatives (XBRL H1-2025 comparative in the Q2-2026 10-Q is unchanged at 60,199), so the ex-Versant FY0 is an analyst estimate; H1-2026 reported (61,396, ex-Versant, incl. Milan-Cortina Olympics + Super Bowl LX) is the cross-check.
inputs.share_count_basis: Q2-2026 weighted-average diluted shares (10-Q filed 2026-07-23). Held FLAT: SBC fully expensed in the flows. Buybacks paused from 1 July 2026 until separation completes, so the count is not expected to fall near-term; period-end count is likely marginally below 3,570 (conservative).
inputs.reported_fcf_definition: FY2025 OCF 33,643 - PP&E capex 11,750 - cash paid for intangibles (capitalised software) 2,658. The CSV FreeCashFlow (21,893) omits the software line and overstates FCF by ~2.7bn/yr.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL ShareBasedCompensation (10-K FY2025 cash flow statement add-back). Taxes withheld on net-share settlement are not separately tagged; excluded, so SBC is slightly understated (immaterial at ~1% of revenue).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Cost of equity 9.0% (10y UST ~4.3% + beta ~0.95 x 5.0% ERP); after-tax cost of debt ~3.9% (marginal pre-tax ~5.1%, 23% tax). Market weights at today's depressed equity price (E ~78bn vs D ~90bn) give ~6.3% - circular and flattering - so a 40% debt / 60% equity target structure is used: 0.6 x 9.0 + 0.4 x 3.9 = 7.0%. Same WACC in all scenarios; risk is carried in the scenario paths and weights, not a premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: lease cost sits inside operating expenses, so EBITDA is already after lease cost. Operating lease liabilities (6,097 at FY2025) are NOT added to net debt. One treatment: leases in the flows.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interests are immaterial (balance 7m at 2026-06-30; NCI share of H1-26 net income -254m, i.e. NCI absorbs losses at Universal Beijing). Ignored.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, scenario-weighted (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company'; first valuation of CMCSA, no prior model decision in memory). Comcast is a US operating company (connectivity + media/parks); not a bank/REIT/holdco. Owner FCF is unlevered: EBITDA (pre-SBC) - SBC - cash tax on EBIT - capex incl. capitalised software; net debt deducted at book in the bridge. FY2025 reported FCF is flattered by abnormally low cash tax (755m vs 5.1-7.1bn in FY2022-24) from OBBBA full expensing - the tax path ramps from ~10% back to 23% of EBIT. The pending mid-2027 NBCU/Sky spin does not change aggregate value to today's holder (they receive both companies); one-off separation costs and dis-synergies sit in the bear margin path. Buybacks: Comcast was a heavy repurchaser (7.2bn FY2025, 2.5bn H1-2026) but is paused from 1 July 2026, so the flat count is currently a convention, not funded. Data: all fundamentals from SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 1166691); no filing text in Extracted/.

equity_bridge.note: XBRL EquityMethodInvestments at 2026-06-30 (Atairos and other affiliates). Their income is below operating income, so it is not in the EBITDA stream; added once here at book.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity and EPS CAGRs are unusable: FY2022 EPS/equity carry the 8.6bn Sky goodwill impairment and FY2025 NI (20.0bn) includes large one-off gains/tax items, while buybacks of 7-13bn/yr shrink equity. Owner-FCF CAGRs (16.6% 3y) are an artefact of FY2025's 755m cash tax (OBBBA). Revenue 3y CAGR (0.6%) is the honest organic anchor; equity CAGR diverges >30% from both revenue and EPS.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (OCF - PP&E - software - SBC): FY2020 11,910; FY2021 15,774; FY2022 11,310; FY2023 11,720; FY2024 11,255; FY2025 17,947. Flat at ~11.3-11.7bn for FY2022-24 despite 36bn of buybacks lifting it per share. SBC grew roughly in line with revenue, so SBC-adjusted and reported FCF CAGRs are close (16.6% vs 15.0% 3y).

base.growth_rationale: FY26 +5% vs ex-Versant FY25: H1-26 +8% incl. Olympics + Super Bowl (~2.6bn event revenue), H2 ~+2% (NBA full season, Epic Universe, wireless vs broadband -5%). FY27 loses the events. FY28 LA Summer Olympics. Thereafter ~1%: broadband revenue decline offset by wireless, business services, parks and Peacock.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: Pre-SBC. FY25 pro forma ~30.6% (36.9bn post-SBC less ~2.4bn Versant EBITDA, +1.3bn SBC); Q2-26 30.6%; H1-26 28.7% with low-margin event revenue. Broadband repricing erodes connectivity margin; Peacock breakeven (was a ~1.5-2bn/yr loss) and parks offset most of it.
base.capex_rationale: PP&E + capitalised software. FY25 11.6% of reported revenue (14.4bn); H1-26 10.6%. Epic Universe build complete; DOCSIS 4.0 / fibre upgrades keep connectivity intensity high.
base.cash_tax_rationale: FY25 cash tax 755m and H1-26 559m (~6% of EBIT) reflect OBBBA full expensing catch-up; FY22-24 ran 5.1-7.1bn. Ramps back to 21% federal + state on unlevered EBIT.

scenario_narratives.base: Broadband keeps losing subscribers to fibre overbuild and T-Mobile/Verizon fixed wireless and domestic broadband revenue falls ~4-5% a year, but converged wireless (record 448k lines in Q2-26), business services, Epic Universe and a now-profitable Peacock roughly offset it: revenue ~1% a year ex-events, pre-SBC EBITDA margin slips from ~30% to 29%, capex stays ~11% of revenue, and cash taxes normalise from the OBBBA trough to 23%. The mid-2027 NBCU/Sky spin is value-neutral in aggregate.
scenario_narratives.bull: Broadband losses peak in 2026-27 as 'irrational' sub-$40 gigabit pricing rationalises and the convergence bundle (wireless penetration of the ~31m broadband base) stems churn; Peacock scales from breakeven to a 1-2bn EBITDA contributor; Epic Universe sustains Orlando attendance; the separation sharpens capital allocation and removes the conglomerate discount. Revenue grows 2-2.5%, margin expands to 31.5%, capex intensity eases to 10.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Broadband enters a full repricing cycle: fibre passings grow 4-5% a year and FWA undercuts on price, subscriber losses worsen (KeyBanc ~665k in 2027) and ARPU falls, so the ~70%-margin connectivity profit pool shrinks year after year. Comcast must keep capex near 11.5-12% to match fibre speeds, theme-park attendance softness persists, linear advertising erodes, and separation adds dis-synergies. Revenue declines 1-3% a year and pre-SBC EBITDA margin compresses to 24% - a harvest business capitalised at 8x with -1% terminal growth.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% because the core profit engine is in structural share loss that management itself says is not improving, and the separation adds execution risk with buybacks paused. Base held at 50% as the most likely path given wireless/Peacock/parks offsets already visible in reported numbers. Bull cut to 20% because it needs broadband stabilisation, Peacock scaling and a clean separation all to go right.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Unlevered owner-FCF DCF on a pro forma ex-Versant base, charging SBC once (flows expensed, count flat), with capitalised software counted as capex and cash taxes normalised from the OBBBA trough. The market at ~8-9x EV/owner-FCF is pricing a long harvest of a shrinking broadband franchise; the model asks how bad that decline must be to justify today's price.
key_risks_to_valuation: Broadband subscriber and ARPU decline steeper than the bear path (fibre + FWA repricing)
Revenue base is an estimate: Versant FY2025 revenue (~6.8bn) and EBITDA (~2.4bn) are not restated in the filings
Cash tax normalisation pace under OBBBA full expensing (each 5pp of cash tax ~ 1bn/yr of FCF)
Separation dis-synergies, one-off costs and leverage allocation between the two companies (mid-2027)
Book value of debt used in the bridge; long-dated low-coupon bonds trade well below par, which would raise equity value on a market-value bridge
Theme-park attendance softness and advertising cyclicality
